title: edikt topic registry (.edikt/topics.yaml)
description: Human-owned, git-versioned map of topic id -> pinned description. Written ONLY by `bin/edikt sidecar approve --kind topic-description` (the approval ceremony) or the owner's own editor; the compile pipeline treats it as read-only input, the same posture parent .md prose gets. Every rendered surface consumes `description` VERBATIM — no rewriting, summarising, or re-deriving.

propertyNames.description: The key IS the topic id — identical pattern to the sidecar `topic` field, so registry keys and sidecar topics join without normalisation.

description.description: ONE task-language line (~25 tokens) stating when a task needs this topic — written for routing ("touching compile internals, sidecar schemas, or render templates"), not taxonomy. Consumed verbatim by the ambient topic index and skill frontmatter.

description_hash.description: Hex SHA-256 of `description`'s exact bytes, stamped by the approval ceremony over the bytes the human actually saw. This is NOT redundant with approved_at: a timestamp alone survives a later edit to the description it was stamped for, so an edited line would keep reading as approved when nobody approved it (pre-flight SEC #7). Detection posture on mismatch is FLAG-and-report, not refuse — an unapproved edit is surfaced with a count and a denominator rather than bricking compile over the owner's own in-progress edit to their own file. No whitespace normalisation before hashing: a normaliser would fold away exactly the changes this field exists to notice.

approved_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp stamped by the approval ceremony. Its presence means a human approved this topic's description; there are no unapproved rows in this file. Pending proposals live in .edikt/state/pending-topic-descriptions/, mirroring the pending-verifies pattern.

compile.description: Changing gov compile, sidecar schemas, Phase A/B internals, or render templates.
